question: A parallel plate capacitor of plate area $2.0 \times 10^{-2}\text{ m}^2$ is being charged. The electric field between the plates changes uniformly at the rate $5.0 \times 10^{10}\text{ V m}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}$. Calculate the displacement current between the plates. Also explain why this current is necessary in describing the charging process.

options.A:
$I_D=\varepsilon_0\dfrac{dE}{dt}=0.4425\text{ A}$.
It is needed because conduction current flows directly across the capacitor gap.
options.B:
$I_D=\varepsilon_0A\dfrac{dE}{dt}=8.85\text{ A}$.
It is unnecessary because current naturally stops at the plates.
options.C:
$I_D=\varepsilon_0A\dfrac{dE}{dt}=(8.85\times10^{-12})(2.0\times10^{-2})(5.0\times10^{10})=8.85\times10^{-3}\text{ A}=8.85\text{ mA}$.
No conduction current crosses the gap, but changing electric flux produces displacement current; it maintains current continuity and makes Ampere's law consistent.
options.D:
$I_D=\dfrac{A}{\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{dE}{dt}=1.13\times10^{20}\text{ A}$.
It is needed because the electric field is constant.
